audits.title: An audit to look at the prescribing of psychotropic medication in the general adult inpatient setting in patients with emotionally unstable personality disorder
audits.setting: Clock View Hospital, general adult inpatient unit, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: EUPD with comorbidity (n=25): 80% on psychotropics before admission, 28% started new medication; 4 of 7 new prescriptions as advised by guidelines. EUPD without comorbidity (n=25): 96% on psychotropics before admission, 28% started new regular medication; 5 of 8 new prescriptions as advised. 78% of 50 prescribed PRN psychotropics; PRN for over one week in 21 patients.

audits.other_findings: Antipsychotic prescribing higher in those without comorbidity (72% vs 60%). Benzodiazepines were the most consistently prescribed PRN medication.
audits.citation: Hyland D, Daniels C, Ionescu I, Houghton C, Goodier K, Graham S. An audit to look at the prescribing of psychotropic medication in the general adult inpatient setting in patients with emotionally unstable personality disorder. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S31-S31. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.136.

audits.title: Audit of pharmacological management of borderline personality disorder as per NICE clinical guidelines CG78
audits.standard: NICE CG78 Borderline personality disorder (eight prescribing, indication and review standards)

cycle1.result: >90% compliance for review of effectiveness and tolerability and no medium/long-term antipsychotic use; <79% for single-drug prescribing, agreeing target symptoms and duration, and written information; 80-89% for sedatives <1 week and discontinuing ineffective treatment.

audits.intervention: Planned: key cards for clinicians, written information for patients, re-audit in 6 months.
audits.citation: Dudley B, Bellam S, Lawrie A. Audit of pharmacological management of borderline personality disorder as per NICE clinical guidelines CG78. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S319-S319. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.841.

audits.title: How Are We Prescribing? a Re-Audit of Prescribing Practices for People With Personality Disorder Presented at the Local Personality Disorder Forums
audits.standard: NICE guidance on drug treatment in borderline personality disorder; two audit standards and four treatment targets from the POMH-UK audit; Trust 'Guidance for Prescribing in Personality Disorder' (Dec 2020)
audits.setting: Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Trust; patients presented at Personality Disorder forums

cycle1.result: Crisis plan documented 87%; clinical reason for antipsychotic documented 43%; antipsychotics >4 weeks without psychosis 86%; Z-hypnotics >4 weeks 13%; benzodiazepines >4 weeks 28%; medication reviews 90%.

audits.intervention: Trust 'Guidance for Prescribing in Personality Disorder' published and circulated across the Trust in December 2020.

cycle2.result: Crisis plan documented 79%; clinical reason for antipsychotic documented 69%; antipsychotics >4 weeks without psychosis 91%; Z-hypnotics >4 weeks 37.5%; benzodiazepines >4 weeks 38%; medication reviews 100% of eligible patients.

audits.other_findings: Quality of medication reviews remained similar to 2017; POMH-UK national audits were done in 2012 and 2014. Findings to be presented with re-emphasis on guidelines and re-audit in 2 years.
audits.citation: Khan M, Reddi N. How Are We Prescribing? a Re-Audit of Prescribing Practices for People With Personality Disorder Presented at the Local Personality Disorder Forums. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(S1):S160-S160. doi:10.1192/bjo.2022.453.

audits.title: An Audit on the Prescribing of Antipsychotics Among People With Recorded Emotionally Unstable Personality Disorder (EUPD) Within a Community Mental Health Service in Stroud, Gloucestershire
audits.standard: NICE guidelines: antipsychotics not recommended for EUPD and should be reviewed with the aim of reducing and stopping
audits.setting: Stroud Recovery community mental health service, Gloucestershire

cycle1.result: 30/37 (81%) with EUPD ever prescribed antipsychotics; 24 (80%) had no licensed comorbid indication. Mean prescription duration 36.79 months in this subgroup; only 10 (42%) reviewed with aim to stop or reduce; none offered a routine physical review.

audits.other_findings: Subgroup was 75% female and 46% aged 20–29; 12 (50%) had more than one antipsychotic, quetiapine most common.
audits.citation: Palermo A, Dibben C. An Audit on the Prescribing of Antipsychotics Among People With Recorded Emotionally Unstable Personality Disorder (EUPD) Within a Community Mental Health Service in Stroud, Gloucestershire. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(S1):S176-S176. doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.461.

audits.title: A Trust Wide Audit Evaluating Prescribing Practices in Clients With Emotionally Unstable Personality Disorder (EUPD)
audits.standard: NICE guidance on EUPD: no drug treatment specifically for EUPD, time-limited crisis prescribing only, regular reviews and written information
audits.setting: South West London and St George's Mental Health NHS Trust, trust-wide

cycle1.result: 81.6% (71) prescribed medication; 39.4% (28) consistent with time-limited prescribing; 57.7% (41) had timely reviews; 4.2% (3) had evidence of written information.

audits.other_findings: Results presented to the Clinical Reference Group and a working group formed to improve prescribing and written information.
audits.citation: Rangan T, Mishra M, Jaura T, Wratten C, White A. A Trust Wide Audit Evaluating Prescribing Practices in Clients With Emotionally Unstable Personality Disorder (EUPD). BJPsych Open. 2023;9(S1):S179-S179. doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.468.
